#Bouquetfire

After the fire is out, there is still work to be done! @ClevelandNF Descanso handcrew is hard at work packing out 43,000 ft of hose used during fire suppression efforts.

This hose will be cleaned, rolled and sent back to the nearest fire support cache for testing and re-issue.

Currently there are fifteen federal National Incident Support Caches that are strategically located across the nation. All supplies in the cache system are managed within the National Fire Equipment System. During a wildfire that goes beyond one shift, firefighting supplies are delivered from the nearest cache to the incident to support fire suppression efforts.

The concept of the “fire cache” dates back to 1900’s. In the early days, the U. S. Forest Service maintained small, pre-positioned wooden boxes containing basic hand tools and canned food in remote areas for employee and public emergency use. Angeles’ Red Box Picnic Area near Mt. Wilson is named after the red box of firefighting tools stored at the site in the early 1900’s.
